top.line: KGELL builds knowledge graphs with LLMs; this newsroom offers its working group 3 309 agent-built graphs in a public vault.
top.para: KGELL, a COST Action running to 2029, aims at an LLM pipeline that builds and refines knowledge graphs while reducing hallucinations. Working group 3 covers construction and an open library of methods. The newsroom's agent built 309 graphs with checked quotes; they, the method and an RDF export are now in a vault, with five offers.

in-short.line: A European network on knowledge graphs and LLMs, its first year, working group 3, and what we offer it.
in-short.para: KGELL runs October 2025 to October 2029. Year one brought a Warsaw meeting, an 88-benchmark catalogue and a Málaga meeting. Working group 3 builds graphs with LLMs. This site's 309 agent-built graphs, checked against their sources, are in a public vault as JSON and RDF, with a method note and five offers.

kgell.line: KGELL is COST Action CA24121, 2025 to 2029, aiming at an LLM pipeline that builds graphs and reduces hallucinations.
kgell.para: Its COST page dates it 23 October 2025 to 22 October 2029, chaired by Diego Reforgiato Recupero with Michael Cochez as vice-chair. It argues LLMs falter in domains, inherit bias and invent facts, and that knowledge graphs supply facts and reasoning. Six working groups split the work.

year-one.line: Year one: a management meeting in Warsaw, D1.1's 88 benchmarks, a Málaga technical meeting and a speaker series.
year-one.para: The first management meeting was on 20 April 2026 in Warsaw. D1.1 catalogues 88 LLM benchmarks across eight features. In Málaga every group reported, and a keynote asked how to evaluate LLM-assisted graph construction. The speaker series continues on 24 November with Claire Gardent and runs into July 2027.

wg3.line: Working group 3 builds knowledge graphs with LLMs and plans an open library of methods and resources.
wg3.para: Led by Ana-Maria Ghiran with Robert Buchmann, both at Babeș-Bolyai University, it covers ontology engineering and schema reuse, LLM extraction of entities and relations, publishing and querying graphs, and linking to Wikidata and DBpedia. Its plan has chapters on guidelines, the role of LLMs, and tools and resources.

fit.line: Fractal semantic graphs and a graph per article make this site's work graph construction with LLMs, in production.
fit.para: The editor joined working group 3 without contributing yet. Fractal semantic graphs keep a vocabulary per domain joined by named edges, schema reuse without one ontology, and are the most-linked article in the site's graphs. Every article also gets a semantic graph, written by the agent that writes it.

graphs.line: 309 graphs with a fixed vocabulary; checks give conformance and verbatim quotes, not faithfulness per triple.
graphs.para: The graphs hold 3,487 nodes of six kinds, 3,386 edges of eight relations and 774 quotes, 7 to 18 nodes each. The writer refuses unknown kinds, relations or topics, missing links, and quotes not word for word. It does not test whether labels, summaries and relations are faithful to the source.

vault.line: A public sgit vault holds the graphs as JSON and RDF, the vocabulary, the method, the offers and statistics.
vault.para: It holds 309 JSON graphs and their index, 21,840 RDF triples in Turtle with an RDFS vocabulary, a method note on what checks catch and miss, a mapping to working group 3's tasks, statistics, and a SPARQL example. Its read key is published so anyone can open or clone it.

offer.line: Five offers: a case study, the dataset, a faithfulness test, Wikidata linking, and vaults for the library.
offer.para: The newsroom offers a case study on agents building graphs per document, the CC BY dataset refreshed as it publishes, an experiment scoring each triple against its source, linking node labels to Wikidata, and versioned, signed vaults as storage for the library. The next step is talking with the group's leads.

limits.line: Public sources only; nothing speaks for KGELL; faithfulness and Wikidata links are not done yet.
limits.para: Everything about KGELL comes from its public pages, the COST page and its memorandum, read on 27 and 28 October 2026. The graphs are one agent's work in one style, their faithfulness unmeasured, with free-text labels. The counts are this site's own.

sources.line: KGELL's pages, the COST page and memorandum, D1.1, and this site's graphs and related articles.
sources.para: Sources are KGELL's home, about, working groups, deliverables, Málaga meeting and speaker series pages, the COST page for CA24121 and its memorandum, D1.1 read in full, and the site's own graphs counted on 28 October 2026, with related articles on fractal semantic graphs and maintained knowledge.
